research_rationale:
Executive Order 11485 of October 1, 1969 (34 FR 15411), Supervision and Control of the National Guard of the District of Columbia, has five sections. Section 1 authorizes and directs the Secretary of Defense to supervise, administer and control the Army and Air National Guard of the District of Columbia while in militia status, with the Commanding General reporting to him and the Secretary able to order out the Guard to aid civil authorities subject to the President's direction. Section 2 makes the Attorney General responsible for advising the President on alternatives for use of the Guard and for establishing law enforcement policies after consultation with the Secretary of Defense. Section 3 provides that the President appoints the Commanding General and the Adjutant General on recommendations of the Secretary of Defense after consultation with the Attorney General. Section 4 authorizes delegation to subordinate officials. Section 5 supersedes Executive Order No. 10030 of January 26, 1949. Sections 1 through 4 are operative on 2026-10-14. Section 5 was performed when the order issued: the order has no effective-date sentence, so I record 1969-10-01, the date of signing (the instrument was filed for publication the same day), as the date of the supersession, with the later Federal Register publication date as the alternative reading. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 11485 finds the order's own Federal Register page, the 1989 OFR codification (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_11485.txt, which prints the five sections with no editorial note) and two source-ladder queue files created for EO 10030; no amendment, revocation or supersession of EO 11485 is held. The OFR executive-order catalog records only that the order supersedes EO 10030. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog (coverage notes read) have no hit for this order, and the packet's term leads for section 1 are report-duty wording, not an end. This is the established route in which the held original, no held later instrument and the three bounded searches support the current predicate; I do not rely on any held current-law text for this order.
